'''Wang Xun''' ({{zh|s=王迅|link=no}}; 23 April 1934 – 5 December 2025) was a Chinese physicist and professor at [[Fudan University]], and an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He was a member of the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP).<ref name="cc"/>

== Life and career ==
Wang was born into a distinguished intellectual family on 23 April 1934, in [[Shanghai]], with his [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] in [[Wuxi]], Jiangsu, to Wang Shouqi, a graduate of National Jiaotong University (now Shanghai Jiao Tong University), and Zhou Miaoqing.<ref name="aa"/> He was a descendant of {{ill|Wang Zai (Qing dynasty)|zh|王縡|lt=Wang Zai}}, who was a politician during the late [[Qing dynasty]] (1644–1911). He had four siblings, two brothers and two sisters.<ref name="aa"/> His elder sister, Wang Jian, was admitted to the pre-medical program of [[Yenching University]] in 1947 and later studied at [[Peking Union Medical College]] and worked at the General Hospital of [[Nanjing Military Region]] after graduation.<ref name="aa"/> His eldest brother, Wang Yu, graduated from the Department of Electrical Engineering of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University|National Jiaotong University]] and later taught at Datong Coal Mining School and the Beijing Coal Mining Cadre Management College.<ref name="aa"/> His younger sister, Wang Jun, enrolled at the Department of Physics at Fudan University and was engaged in work related to [[nuclear physics]].<ref name="aa"/> His youngest brother, [[Wang Xuan (computer scientist)|Wang Xuan]], was an academician of both the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the [[Chinese Academy of Engineering]] (CAE).<ref name="aa"/> 

Xun attended [[Shanghai Nanyang Model High School]].<ref name="cc" /> In 1952, he  entered the Department of Physics at [[Fudan University]], earning his bachelor's degree in 1956.<ref name="bb" /><ref name="cc" /> He continued his graduate studies at Fudan under the supervision of the renowned physicist [[Xie Xide]], graduating in 1960 and subsequently joining the faculty.<ref name="bb" /><ref name="cc" />

Wang's research career was centered at Fudan University, where he dedicated over six decades.<ref name="bb"/><ref name="cc"/> He was promoted to associate professor in May 1978 and to full professor in August 1984.<ref name="bb"/><ref name="cc"/> From March to November 1980, he was a visiting professor at the [[University of Wisconsin Milwaukee]] in the United States. He held several key leadership positions, including director of the Surface Physics Laboratory and the founding director of the State Key Laboratory of Applied Surface Physics, which he helped establish with Xie Xide in 1992.<ref name="bb"/><ref name="cc"/>

On 5 December 2025, Wang died in Shanghai at the age of 91.<ref name="cc"/><ref>{{cite news |editor1=Yang Pingya ({{lang|zh|杨雅萍}}) |url=https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20251206A06D0E00 |script-title=zh:痛别！王迅院士逝世 |work=Tencent |date=6 December 2025 |access-date=8 December 2025 |language=zh}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
* 1999 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS)<ref name="cc"/>
* 2002 State Natural Science Award (First Class) for the research on the development, physical properties, and preparation of new devices of silicon based low dimensional structural materials.<ref name="cc"/>
